Connectedness is not used. Mixed E_{>=0}-manifolds included

hypotheses.paper: « For alpha > 0 the singular line is timelike, hence locally chronal » (l.1341), read in M
hypotheses.note: a reading (see questions): sing_locallyChronal (in every open W containing p ∈ sing_kappa(M), a chronal curve of W through p inside sing_kappa(M), its points <<_W-related) and component_timelike (two points of a component are equal or <<-related in M)

in a reading: Causal.E0 (OQ-34, OQ-35), entering through the cover's family and the cross-type invariance E_0 <-> E_kappa (SFALocal.mem_sing_iff_of_mem_source); Flat.isom 2 = SO_0(1,2) ⋉ R^3 (OQ-82), entering through prop_isom_local

findings: ETT.tex:1341 (« for alpha > 0 the singular line is timelike, hence locally chronal ») read in M, and lem:past_BTZ (a) for alpha > 0 (l.1518-1519): proved at every Hausdorff E_{>=0}-manifold, in the readings DEC-25, OQ-18, OQ-34/35 and OQ-82, with no absolute minimality, no second countability and no connectedness. Each component of sing_alpha(M), alpha > 0, is the range of a gamma : R -> M with gamma 0 = p, an inextensible chronal curve, a closed embedding when C is causal (Causal.SFAMassiveLine.massive_line, exactly the field SingularFlatAxioms.massive_line). Locally: through each point of sing_kappa(M), every open set W containing it contains a chronal curve of W inside sing_kappa(M) whose points are <<_W-related (sing_locallyChronal). Globally: two points of one component are equal or chronologically related in M (component_timelike). Non-vacuous at M = E_pi: sing_pi(E_pi) = singLine pi ≠ ∅, and the line through (0, apex) is a closed embedding onto the whole singular line (nonvacuous_epi).

ETT.tex:1529-1533 (proof of (a)), for alpha > 0. The route through prop:GX_sing_dec (l.1435-1437, a closed smooth 1-submanifold) and « since M is a differential manifold, it is parametrisable by R » (l.1530) is not needed. The time coordinate of the X_A-charts into E_kappa is a translation atlas of sing_kappa(M), because near the line two such charts differ by a time translation times a rotation (BTZ_1 prop:isom, local form, BPrimeEAlpha.prop_isom_local). That fact also settles a point the proof leaves implicit: « locally chronal » gives « a chronal curve » (l.1531-1533) only for a parametrisation that is future-directed in every chart. The translation transitions never reverse time, so the chart time orients the whole component. Hausdorff (l.255) is used (uniqueness of line arcs, LineDevelopment.exists_development). « Parametrisable by R » is a homeomorphism onto the component only when M is causal. A compact component is the image of a periodic gamma (abstract witness LineDevelopment.circle_line). By hand, not formalized: E_kappa modulo the time translation rotShift T 0 has a circle as sing_kappa. This is why the field asks for a closed embedding only when C is causal; T-ett-line-development made the same observation at alpha = 0.

Roadmap, not the paper (the planner's [r] notes in T-ett-sfa-massive-line). (1) Every cited location is correct: SFALocal.sing_pos :284, sing_two_pi :386, eq_of_mem_singAt :251, SingularFlat.lean:150-169 and :203-206, Massive.lean:148 and :162, MassiveManifold.lean:111, BPrimeEAlpha.lean:1098. (2) The route is confirmed. tau is the time coordinate x.1, sigma r = e.symm (r, apex), J = {r | (r, apex) ∈ e.target}, and Sing ∩ source = e⁻¹(singLine kappa) by IsAEChart.mem_reg_iff and EAlphaGX.sing_eq (mem_sing_iff_mem_singLine). One application of prop_isom_local to e.symm.trans e' gives the transitions on a whole neighbourhood of x: the clause y ∈ S of IsTranslationAtlas.trans is not used. (3) Three steps are already inside LineDevelopment.exists_chronal_line, so this file does not use them separately: injectivity « as in T-ett-sfa-line-e0 » (it is injective_of_isCausal with IsLineDevelopment.locallyInjective), CurveOn.comp_strictMonoOn and the locality (8). The only per-chart input is that sigma e is chronal over every segment of J e (chronalCurveOn_lineσ: singLine_chronalCurveOn through ChartIso.curveOn_symm with the lt family). (4) « E_0 plays no part » is not exact. A chart of the cover at a point of sing_kappa(M) may a priori go into E_0. It is excluded by the cross-type invariance E_0 <-> E_kappa (SFALocal.mem_sing_iff_of_mem_source, through MassAModelsInstance.source_subset_reg_of_isAEChart_e0_massive). So the hypothesis involves E_0 and OQ-34/OQ-35 apply, as the dispatch's marks say. (5) Step 5 fits. With massive_line proved, SingularFlatAxioms at a Hausdorff, second countable E_{>=0}-manifold is equivalent to the BTZ field line alone (singularFlatAxioms_iff_line). It holds with no BTZ point (singularFlatAxioms_of_sing_zero; singularFlatAxioms_of_massive for E_{>0}-manifolds). E_pi is the library's first SingularFlatAxioms witness with a non-empty massive line (epi_singularFlatAxioms): every earlier instance has sing_alpha = ∅ for alpha > 0 (CBG.lean:390, E0SingularFlat.lean:289, SFALocalE0.lean:429, SingularFlat.lean:610).
questions: What is defi:causal_Ealpha's last sentence (ETT.tex:1341, « For alpha > 0 the singular line is timelike, hence locally chronal ») a statement of? As printed, it is about the model E_alpha (Definition « of the model spaces »). The proof of lem:past_BTZ (a) uses it at M (l.1531, « locally chronal by Definition defi:causal_Ealpha »). Reading taken: at the model it remains Causal.singLine_lt / singLine_locallyChronal (strict, already in the row). At M it is the local form sing_locallyChronal plus the global forms massive_line (chronal over every segment) and component_timelike, all proved here. « Locally chronal » at M is read as follows: in every open W containing p, a chronal curve of W (DEC-6) through p inside sing_kappa(M), its points <<_W-related. This mirrors the model's singLine_locallyChronal. This is the counterpart of the question T-ett-sfa-btz-e0 raised for defi:causal_E0.

kb_proposals: The translation atlas of sing_kappa(M), kappa > 0, kappa ≠ 2π (Causal.SFAMassiveLine.isTranslationAtlas): index the X_A-charts into E_kappa that are ChartIso (IsoChart C kappa, a subtype, under attribute [local instance] EAlphaGX.singularGX), with tau = (e ·).1, sigma r = e.symm (r, apex), J = {r | (r, apex) ∈ e.target}. The transition is one prop_isom_local on e.symm.trans e' plus BPrimeEAlpha.exists_polar for the point. A cover chart at p ∈ sing_kappa(M) lands in IsoChart after rcases o with _ | ⟨κ', hκ'⟩ and subst (κ' = κ from SFALocal.mem_sing_iff_of_mem_source). The family terms massAModelSingularGX (some κ) and massAModelCausality (some κ) are accepted by exact as EAlphaGX.singularGX κ and massive κ (Fact is a Prop).

Pitfall: inside namespace Causal.X with open SFALocal, an unqualified isClosed_sing resolves to the strict root Causal.isClosed_sing (every singular (G,X)-manifold, explicit G X M), not to SFALocal.isClosed_sing. The error is « expected Type ». Write SFALocal.isClosed_sing.

E_pi is a SingularFlatAxioms witness with a non-empty massive line: Causal.SFAMassiveLine.epi_singularFlatAxioms (from SFALocal.nonvacuous_epi and singularFlatAxioms_of_sing_zero). Use it to instantiate theorems that take SingularFlatAxioms with sing_alpha ≠ ∅, alpha > 0, e.g. CBG.exists_massive_near (CBG/FromModel.lean:1694).
